name: Waif
summary: This article is about the Coquette sub-aesthetic.
description:
This article is about the Coquette sub-aesthetic. For the anime "femcel" aesthetic, see Femcel .

Waif , also known as Girlblogger, Female Manipulator, or Femcel, is an internet aesthetic and persona within the Coquette sphere. It revolves around a modern archetype of a young woman who is intelligent, misunderstood, beautiful, and emotionally troubled, often exhibiting self-destructive, toxic, or manipulative tendencies. The imagery of the aesthetic reflects that complex lifestyle, emphasizing both its chaotic nature and its aspirational qualities.

The Waif aesthetic is one of many that developed out of the Heroin Chic trend and its cultural influence over womanhood. Waif draws significant inspiration from the Dark Nymphet, Sadgirl and pro-ana communities. Some of the defining features of this aesthetic are its relation to media about unlikable, flawed female protagonists and a cynical, detached sense of humor (partially inspired by the podcast Red Scare ). Waif content is not limited to curated images; it is also heavily conveyed through memes, mood boards, anonymous confessions on the app Whisper, and text posts about users' personal lives.

While it shares visuals with many Coquette-related aesthetics, its unique embrace of controversial values and viewpoints, unashamed portrayal of mental illness, and acceptance of toxic personality traits sets it apart.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Preoccupation with beauty and thinness, performative narcissism, intellectual pretension, embracing "unlikable" traits and female protagonists
